_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and the input file x21-re-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or API was used.

hints.reason: ARM via the garment sleeve that covers it; TATTOO via the well-known 'sleeve' tattoo that covers an arm: a clean double meaning with a nice click.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair; SLEEVE is the natural best hint.

hints.reason: BAG via the Coach handbag brand; WHISTLE via the sports coach's whistle: brand plus role, a satisfying swerve.

pairs.pair_note: Strong brand/role double meaning.

hints.reason: BASE via sliding into a base; SAFE via the umpire's 'safe' call after a slide: one vivid baseball scene, easy but satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Clear baseball scene; easy, fair.

hints.reason: BATH via the bathrobe; JUDGE via the judicial black robe: the same garment word in two very different settings.

pairs.pair_note: Solid, fair two-setting hint.

hints.reason: BIRD via the sparrow songbird; JACK via Captain Jack Sparrow: an instant pop-culture double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Great pop-culture double meaning.

hints.reason: BOARD via Battleship the board game; SINK via 'You sank my battleship!' and sinking the fleet: classic and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Classic game reference; good.

hints.reason: BOTTLE via the bottle opener; SEASON via the season opener game or episode: two familiar compounds with different senses.

pairs.pair_note: Clean double meaning; very good.

hints.reason: GENIUS via 'an Einstein' meaning a genius; BRAIN via Einstein as the archetypal big brain (and his famously preserved brain): fair, if easy.

pairs.pair_note: The preserved-brain fact is true but the hint works even without it, since Einstein is shorthand for brains.

hints.reason: BUG via a software bug; VIRUS via a computer virus: both words shift from biology to computing, a straightforward but tidy link.

pairs.pair_note: Obvious but sound; GERM would be a weaker alternative.

hints.reason: CABBAGE and KID both sit in the instantly familiar 'Cabbage Patch Kids' doll name: a phrase-join that genuinely delights with nostalgia.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but the brand is instant and the pairing is fun.

hints.reason: DYNAMITE via the lit fuse on a stick; CANNON via the classic (especially cartoon) image of lighting a cannon's fuse: fair and widely recognised.
hints.fix: Old cannons were fired by putting a flame to the touch hole, and cannons in cartoons are classically lit by a fuse.

pairs.pair_note: Route is fine; the CANNON line slightly overstates fuses (historic guns were usually fired with a slow match or linstock at the touch hole).

hints.reason: CAR via driving a car; THUMB via a thumb drive: a neat double meaning with a small aha on the THUMB side.

pairs.pair_note: Good double meaning.

hints.reason: CHAMPAGNE via the champagne flute glass; INSTRUMENT via the woodwind flute: a classic, satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning.

hints.reason: CHEF via Remy the rat chef in Pixar's film; FRANCE via the Paris setting and the French stew: film and dish reinforce each other.

pairs.pair_note: Great film/food reference.

hints.reason: CINDERELLA via the glass slipper; FOOT via the slipper fitting her foot: an iconic story moment, easy and fair.
hints.fix: In the story, the glass slipper is tried on young women's feet until it fits Cinderella.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the FOOT line says the prince tries it on every maiden, but in the best-known (Disney) version the Grand Duke does the fitting and 'each maiden' is an overstatement.

hints.reason: CLOWN via the jester as a clown-like fool; COURT via the familiar phrase 'court jester': near-synonym on one side but an honest, instant second link.

pairs.pair_note: Near-synonym of CLOWN, but 'court jester' makes the second link genuine.

hints.reason: COUNTRY via the country club; GOLF via the golf club you swing (and the golf club as a venue): a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning.

hints.reason: PIE via 'eat humble pie'; CROW via 'eat crow', which means the same humbling act: two idioms with one meaning, a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Indirect idiom route with a genuine payoff; strong.

hints.reason: DANCE via prom as the formal school dance; DRESS via the prom dress: obvious but a clean, satisfying fit.
hints.fix: A prom is a formal school dance, and a prom dress is the formal gown worn to it.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair; explanation wording ('picking a prom dress is a big part of the night') is a little muddled since shopping happens before the night.

hints.reason: DEAD via a dead battery; PHONE via the phone battery that dies: an everyday scene that clicks immediately.

pairs.pair_note: Solid everyday hint.

hints.reason: SHOWER via a meteor shower; DINOSAUR via the space-rock impact popularly pictured as a meteor wiping them out: indirect familiar knowledge with a nice twist.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the DINOSAUR line is carefully hedged (asteroid impact, 'often pictured as a giant meteor').

hints.reason: DROP via the cartoon anvil dropped on a character; HEAVY via the anvil as the archetypal heavy object: a fun, vivid gag.

pairs.pair_note: Fun cartoon scene.

hints.reason: ELASTIC via the stretchy bungee cord; JUMP via the bungee jump: direct and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Straightforward, fair.

hints.reason: FAMILY via the Parr family at the heart of the film; SUPERHERO via their superpowers: a well-loved Pixar reference that hits both cleanly.

pairs.pair_note: Great reference; the hint is a title, not a plural of a target.

hints.reason: PHOENIX via rising from its own ashes; FLAME via flames leaving ashes (and the phoenix bursting into flame): fair, with the legend tying both together.

pairs.pair_note: Fair legend link; FLAME side is a little generic but the phoenix story binds it.

hints.reason: FORK via the tuning fork; GUITAR via tuning the strings (a tuning fork can even be used to tune one): fair and coherent.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; the shared musical context makes it more than a bare phrase-join.

hints.reason: FRIEND and WEATHER both come from the familiar idiom 'fair-weather friend', and 'fair weather' stands on its own too: an instant, satisfying phrase-join.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but the idiom is instantly familiar and the fit is neat.

hints.reason: GIANT via the giants of Brobdingnag (and Gulliver as a giant in Lilliput); SMALL via the tiny Lilliputians: the story's whole point is the two scales, a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Lovely use of the story's two lands; lines are accurate.

hints.reason: GOD via Mercury the Roman messenger god; THERMOMETER via the liquid mercury in older thermometers: a classic double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; note MERCURY is also used for METAL + PLANET in this batch, so avoid serving both in the same session.

hints.reason: HARD and LIFE both come from Annie's famous song 'It's the Hard Knock Life': a step removed from a bare phrase-join, with a pleasant aha.

pairs.pair_note: Good; KNOCK would be a plainer phrase-join alternative, ANNIE is more fun.

hints.reason: INSTRUMENT via the harp; SEAL via the harp seal with its famous white pups: fair, though the harp seal is moderately rather than universally known.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; harp seal is well enough known from wildlife imagery.

hints.reason: NEW via 'New Zealand'; KIWI via the kiwi bird and Kiwis as New Zealanders' nickname: easy, clean and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; the NEW side is a pure phrase-join but KIWI gives it substance.

hints.reason: LIFE via a 1-Up being an extra life; MARIO via the green 1-Up Mushroom: an instant, fun gaming reference.

pairs.pair_note: Great gaming hint; digit-hyphen spelling is allowed.

hints.reason: METAL via the liquid metal mercury; PLANET via Mercury closest to the Sun: textbook double meaning, easy but clean.

pairs.pair_note: Clean but obvious; MERCURY also serves GOD + THERMOMETER in this batch.

hints.reason: MODEL via models posing; STRIKE via 'strike a pose' (Madonna's Vogue): a clean pairing with a fun pop echo.

pairs.pair_note: Good; idiom plus job.

hints.reason: NEW via New Jersey; SPORT via the team jersey: a neat state-name versus shirt double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Good double meaning.

hints.reason: PASS via 'Do not pass Go'; PRISON via Monopoly's Jail: the famous Go-to-Jail card ties both in one instruction.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; PRISON maps to Jail cleanly.

hints.reason: PLATE via tectonic plates; VOLCANO via volcanoes forming at plate boundaries (Ring of Fire): accurate school science, fair.

pairs.pair_note: Fair science hint; accurate text.

hints.reason: ROCK via stones as rocks (and the Rolling Stones as a rock band); TONGUE via the Stones' iconic tongue-and-lips logo: a satisfying aha once Rolling Stones lands.

pairs.pair_note: Nice indirect route; the tongue logo is iconic.

hints.reason: SEAL and STAMP via the parallel idioms 'seal of approval' and 'stamp of approval': both instantly familiar and meaning the same, so the pairing satisfies.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but two parallel stock idioms make it clean.

hints.reason: SKIN via a mole on the skin; SPY via a mole planted in an organization: a classic double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning.

hints.reason: TOILET via Charmin toilet paper; SOFT via its long-running softness advertising and Ultra Soft line: a familiar brand hint, PG.

pairs.pair_note: Fair brand hint.

hints.reason: SWING via the tire swing; TREE via the tire swing hung from a branch: one nostalgic backyard image, easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair scene.

hints.reason: WHITE via the band The White Stripes (and the zebra's literal white stripes); ZEBRA via its black-and-white stripes: the band name and the animal reinforce each other.

pairs.pair_note: Band-name phrase-join, but the zebra's literal white stripes make it click.
